Who collects delinquent property tax in Nassau County

The Nassau County Treasurer collects delinquent tax for the whole county at 1 West Street in Mineola. The phone number is 516-571-2090, and hours are 9:00 am to 4:30 pm, Monday through Friday. Current bills are handled by the receiver of taxes in your town, but once a balance turns delinquent it moves to the county's Tax Records unit.

The scope depends on where you live. For the Towns of Hempstead, North Hempstead and Oyster Bay, the Treasurer takes both general and school delinquencies. The City of Glen Cove handles its own school tax delinquencies, so only its general tax comes to the county, and for the City of Long Beach the county takes school tax plus only the county portion of the general tax.

  • Delinquent school tax collection starts June 1; delinquent general tax collection starts September 1.
  • Always write the parcel section, block and lot on any check.
  • Checks go to the Nassau County Treasurer, 1 West Street, Mineola, NY 11501, or into the lobby drop-box.

2026 delinquent tax payment deadlines

For 2026 delinquent taxes, personal checks are accepted from June 1 through November 30, 2026, and online credit card or electronic check payments from June 26, 2026 through January 31, 2027. The last day to pay before the lien sale is Wednesday, February 10, 2027 at 3:00 PM.

Online payments carry small charges: $0.45 for an electronic check and a 2.3% bank charge for a credit card. The ACH limit is $99,999.99 and the card limit is $25,000. Tax liens already sold are different. They cannot be paid online and need a bank cashier's check or cash.

How does the Nassau County tax lien sale work?

Instead of foreclosing right away, Nassau County sells its unpaid tax liens each February at a public online auction. On February 16, 2027 the Treasurer will sell the 2026 liens on parcels whose balance has not been paid by February 10.

Bidders pay a $175 registration fee and a $5,000 minimum deposit, then 10% of the purchase is due the day of the sale and the remaining 90% by March 18. A bidder who misses the 90% balance deadline forfeits winning bids and the deposit. If you own a parcel on the list, February 10 is the date that matters most to you.

How to appeal a Nassau County assessment

Nassau County appeals go to the Assessment Review Commission, which is independent of the Department of Assessment, and the next filing window runs from January 4, 2027 to March 1, 2027. No fee is charged to file for yourself, and the Commission can lower an assessment or leave it as is, but it cannot raise it. The Treasurer's office also refunds tax certiorari awards and settlements, which is the money side of a successful appeal.

Timing is slower than many owners expect. Assessments published in January become final on the first business day of April of the following year, and they feed school tax bills in October of that year and general tax bills in the January after that. A reduction won now therefore reaches your bill well after you file, and a seller who closes first may leave the benefit to the buyer.

Filing is online through AROW, which the county prefers over paper. The Commission's questions line is 516-571-3214. Three forms exist: AR1 for a one-, two- or three-family home, AR2 for other property, and AR3 for tax class or exemption disputes. Appeals take up to fifteen months, with determinations by March 31 of the year after you file.

  • Class 1 homes cannot see a total assessment rise more than 6% in a year or 20% in five years, except for construction or renovation.
  • Village, Glen Cove and Long Beach assessments are appealed locally, and an ARC filing does not protect those rights.
  • If you reject an offered reduction, owner-occupied homes can pursue small claims review after the final roll on the first business day of April.

Nassau County housing at a glance

Nassau County is dense and expensive. Estimates for July 2025 show 1,398,939 residents across 284.54 square miles of land, with 480,591 housing units. Owners occupy 81.9% of homes, the median owner-occupied value is $684,700, median household income is $146,202, and median gross rent is $2,252.

Mineola is the county seat. The county is divided into two cities, three towns and 64 incorporated villages, and it has 58 public school districts whose boundaries do not match village or postal lines. That patchwork explains why two houses on the same street can carry different school bills. For a seller with a delinquent bill, the date matters most: a sale that fails to close before February 10 leaves the 2026 lien exposed to the February 16 auction.

What are my options if I owe Nassau County tax and want to sell?

Request the current balance by parcel from the Treasurer and see whether your lien has been sold already. The Treasurer's unpaid tax listings page carries monthly updated delinquent tax files. A sale that closes before February 10 pays the balance from proceeds, which stops the lien from going to auction.

A buyer paying cash and taking the house as it is can close faster than a financed buyer, and speed is what protects you against the lien-sale calendar. If you think your assessment is too high, filing with ARC in early 2027 can reduce the next bill whether or not you sell, and a pending sale does not prevent you from filing.

  1. Get a payoff in writing from the Treasurer, 516-571-2090.
  2. Check whether your parcel is in a village, Glen Cove or Long Beach, since delinquent tax rules differ there.
  3. Set a closing date before February 10, 2027 if the 2026 tax is still open.

If a lien has already been sold, the rules change. A sold lien cannot be paid online, so you would need a bank cashier's check or cash, and the Treasurer can tell you how to pay it. Bring your parcel section, block and lot to every call and ask for each figure in writing. A written payoff lets the closing attorney and title company confirm exactly what comes out of proceeds, which keeps the closing on schedule.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay delinquent taxes in Nassau County?

Pay the Nassau County Treasurer, either online at the county's delinquent tax page or by check to 1 West Street, Mineola, NY 11501. Include your parcel section, block and lot. Help with online payments is at 516-571-2090.

What is the last day to pay 2026 delinquent tax before the lien sale?

Wednesday, February 10, 2027, at 3:00 PM. The lien auction itself is on February 16, 2027, and the county will sell the 2026 liens on any parcels that remain unpaid.

When can I appeal my Nassau County assessment?

From January 4, 2027 through March 1, 2027, through the Assessment Review Commission's online AROW system or on paper. No extension is available after March 1.

Can the Assessment Review Commission raise my assessment?

No. It can reduce the assessment or leave it unchanged. Filing yourself costs nothing, and you do not have to hire a representative.

Does Nassau County foreclose directly on unpaid tax?

The county holds an annual tax lien sale each February, where liens on unpaid taxes are sold at online auction. Ask the Treasurer how a sold lien is handled for your parcel.

Which office collects Suffolk County property tax?

A Receiver of Taxes in each of the ten towns collects Suffolk County's combined town, school and county bill from December 1 through May 31, and the County Comptroller collects whatever is still unpaid after that. The ten towns are Babylon, Brookhaven, East Hampton, Huntington, Islip, Riverhead, Shelter Island, Smithtown, Southampton and Southold. Your town Assessor sets the assessed value, and the Receiver in your town issues the bill.

Suffolk is the easternmost county in New York and takes up the eastern two-thirds of Long Island. The county seat is Riverhead, though most county offices are in Hauppauge. It was one of twelve original counties created in 1683. The Comptroller's collection office is at 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901, with administrative hours that start at 9:00 a.m. and finish at five in the afternoon, and counter payments ending at 4:15 p.m. The main number is 631-852-3000.

  • Town Receiver of Taxes: bills, duplicate bills and payments through May 31.
  • Town Assessor: value, exemptions and mailing-address changes.
  • County Comptroller: delinquent tax, bankruptcies, refunds of overpayment, tax liens and redemption statements.

Which Suffolk County towns have the most homes to tax?

Brookhaven is the largest of the ten towns by a wide margin, followed by Islip, Babylon, Huntington and Smithtown. The county's town list shows these populations:

  • Brookhaven: 488,497
  • Islip: 337,922
  • Babylon: 217,656
  • Huntington: 203,243
  • Smithtown: 115,768
  • Riverhead: 35,834
  • East Hampton: 28,607
  • Southold: 23,912
  • Southampton: 69,490
  • Shelter Island: 3,276

Suffolk also has 32 incorporated villages, from Amityville and Babylon to Sag Harbor and Westhampton Beach. The county also lists dozens of school districts, among them Brentwood, Commack, Half Hollow Hills and Hampton Bays. Ask your town Receiver which town, school and other levies make up the bill for your parcel.

What is the Suffolk County tax year and when is the bill due?

The tax year runs December 1 to November 30 of the following year, and bills are mailed by the town Receivers around mid-December. Pay the first half by January 10 to avoid interest. After that, 1 percent a month applies to the first half until May 31. The second half is payable without interest through May 31.

One detail trips up people who buy in spring. Suffolk's own notice tells anyone who buys property during the year to find out whether the second-half tax has been paid, because the new owner is the one who has to deal with it. Another is that exemptions granted to the previous owner, such as a veterans or senior exemption, do not pass to the buyer, so the first bill after a sale can be much higher.

Partial payments of at least $200 are accepted by both the Receiver and the Comptroller. Interest and penalties are charged on the unpaid balance only, and accepting a partial payment does not waive the County's lien rights on what remains.

What happens to Suffolk taxes unpaid after May 31?

They become delinquent, payable to the County Comptroller, with a 5 percent penalty and interest of 1 percent a month counted from February 1 on the tax plus penalty. A tax sale advertising fee is added to anything still unpaid after August 31. The Comptroller's own example shows a $1,000 tax growing to $1,050 with the penalty and to $1,102.50 if paid by June 30.

Interest added to delinquent Suffolk County tax by month of payment (source: Suffolk County Comptroller Information for Taxpayers)
Month paidInterest rate
June5%

September8%

Mail a delinquent payment to the Suffolk County Comptroller, 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901, with the property description exactly as it reads on the tax bill or deed.

Does Suffolk County take the house if the tax stays unpaid?

Not at once. If tax is still unpaid on the date of the lien sale, usually held in November or December, the Comptroller sells the County a tax lien against the parcel. Before that sale, the list of liens runs for six weeks in the official newspapers and for two weeks in a newspaper in each of the ten towns.

After the sale the owner can clear the lien by paying the lien amount, accrued interest and any later County taxes through an application to the Comptroller. The window is twelve months from the sale date, and thirty-six months if the parcel is assessed as a one-, two- or three-family residence. Redemption statements covering every open lien are available from the Comptroller on request.

When the period runs out the County issues a tax deed. Redeeming after that point means applying to the Suffolk County Department of Planning, Division of Real Estate, at 631-853-5900. The Comptroller's contact page lists that same number for redemption of property taken by tax deed.

What should I do after buying a house or paying off a mortgage in Suffolk?

Contact your local Receiver of Taxes right away. The County says a new owner should get a current bill and learn what is due next and when. An owner who has just satisfied a mortgage with taxes in escrow should ask the Receiver to send future bills straight to the owner, then confirm the next payment date and mailing address.

  • Ask whether the second-half tax on the parcel has been paid.
  • Ask the Assessor to correct the mailing address, since the Assessor drives the roll that bills come from.
  • Check whether a bank paid the whole year when a mortgage ended mid-year. The bank is not obliged to forward a bill.
  • Keep records of any exemption you hope to claim by March 1.

For refunds of overpaid tax, bankruptcy questions and court-ordered reductions or corrections of error, the Comptroller's office uses the same main number, 631-852-3000.

Where do I dispute a Suffolk County assessment?

Bring your complaint to your town's review board on Grievance Day, the third Tuesday in May, which is May 18 in 2027. The board must sit for at least four hours. The county assessment calendar the Comptroller publishes runs in this order:

  • January 1: valuation date.
  • March 1: taxable status date, and the deadline for all exemption filings.
  • Third Tuesday in May: Grievance Day.
  • July 1: final roll, with taxes extended from it.

If the board does not give you relief, a small claims petition has a 30-day clock that starts when the final roll is filed. To qualify you need to have filed a written complaint with the Board of Assessment Review and live in a one-, two- or three-family house used only as a residence. Your town Assessor, not the County, holds the assessment file.

What do Suffolk County housing numbers look like for a seller?

Suffolk is expensive and owner-heavy. Census QuickFacts for 2020-2024 put the median home value at $578,400, with 82.2 percent of homes lived in by their owners, across 512,565 households. Median household income is $130,686, and renters pay a median of $2,255 in gross rent. The county estimate for July 2025 is 1,546,090 people, up from 1,525,920 at the 2020 census.

Geography shapes risk. The county covers 2,373 square miles, of which only 912 are land, with roughly 980 miles of coastline and a high point of 401 feet at Jayne's Hill. Because so much of the housing sits near sea level, buyers often ask for flood and drainage history. Pull your insurance records and any elevation certificate before you list.

Frequently asked questions

Who do I pay Suffolk County property tax to before May 31?

The Receiver of Taxes in your town. Taxes are payable there from December 1 to May 31, and after that date they go to the County Comptroller.

How long can I redeem a Suffolk County tax lien?

Twelve months from the lien sale, or thirty-six months for a one-, two- or three-family residence. After that the County issues a tax deed.

Is a mailed Suffolk tax payment accepted by postmark?

Yes, by the USPS postmark on the envelope. A metered postmark is not accepted, so use certified or registered mail near a deadline.

What if I never received my Suffolk County tax bill?

You still owe the tax plus any penalty and interest. Ask your town Receiver of Taxes for a duplicate bill right away.

Does a Suffolk tax exemption move to the buyer of my house?

No. A veterans or senior exemption stays with the person who received it, so the buyer's first tax bill can be higher than yours was.

Who collects property tax in Westchester County, NY?

Your city or town collects it, and the county does not. The Westchester County Tax Commission says plainly that the county takes no property tax payments directly from owners and asks people not to mail it checks. The 25 cities and towns also bill and collect the county's share, then guarantee and forward the total to the county's Finance Department.

Westchester covers six cities, 19 towns and 23 villages in the Hudson Valley, with White Plains as the county seat. Yonkers is the largest municipality. Because bills, assessment records and tax history all live at the local level, the first call about a bill always goes to the municipality where the house sits.

  • City or town receiver of taxes: bills, payments, balances and payoff letters.
  • Local assessor: value, exemptions and name changes.
  • County Finance Department, 148 Martine Avenue, White Plains: county tax refunds after a small claims reduction. The Commissioner of Finance is also the county treasurer.
  • County Tax Commission, 110 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd., Room L-346, White Plains, phone 914-995-4325: general property tax questions and equalization data.

What does the Westchester County Tax Commission do?

It spreads the county levy fairly among the municipalities and trains local assessment staff. The Commission reviews local assessment rolls each year for that purpose, orients new assessors, trains Board of Assessment Review members, reviews applications to correct tax and assessment errors, and publishes an annual report on assessments, equalization, exemptions and tax rates.

The Commission does not set individual assessments, collect current or delinquent tax, or take part in lien sales and foreclosure. Those jobs belong to the towns, cities and villages. The county describes its own property taxes as among the highest in the nation, which is one reason local grievance deadlines matter to a seller.

When are Westchester property taxes due?

The date depends on the municipality, and the county publishes a chart of the last day to pay without penalty. County tax is due once a year in April, May or June in most of the cities below, and Peekskill splits it in two, while city, town and school bills follow their own calendars. A village adds a fourth bill in some places.

Who runs tax lien sales in Westchester County?

The city or town where the property sits runs them, since the county Finance Department states that it does not conduct delinquent property tax lien sales. The cities and towns also pursue collection against owners who fall behind, so a balance that looks old can still be enforced locally.

State law gives the outline for a delinquent parcel. A lien can be redeemed by paying the amount due plus legal charges, and the redemption period under RPTL 1110 ends two years after the lien date unless a notice or a local choice changes it. Legal charges can include notice costs, interest and penalties, and an allowance of up to $250 or 2 percent of the amount due on a parcel, whichever is greater, under RPTL 1102.

Local rules differ. Yonkers charges 15 percent annual interest from the confirmation date with no grace period, and White Plains charges 1 percent a month on overdue tax. Ask the municipality that holds your lien what its sale schedule is, and whether any notices have been mailed.

How does a Westchester small claims reduction turn into a refund?

After you win a Small Claim Assessment Review in court, your municipality has to complete a county refund form, and the county aims to process its portion within 90 days after it has all the paperwork. The form needs signatures from the assessor and the receiver of taxes, plus a copy of the court decision or the settlement signed by the hearing officer.

The municipality mails the package to the County Finance Department, Attn: SCAR Processing, 148 Martine Avenue, Suite 724, White Plains, NY 10601. The refund check goes to the owner's address, or to the address on the court order. The county says it cannot process incomplete paperwork, and it can speak only to the county portion of the refund. Ask your city, town or school district about refunds of local tax.

The tool is meant for residential owners. If you plan to sell, tell the title company about any pending SCAR result and ask who receives a refund that arrives after closing.

What do Census figures say about Westchester County homes?

1,015,743 residents for July 2025 and 399,598 housing units. About 61.8 percent of households own their home. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $663,200 for 2020 to 2024, and median household income is $118,976.

Owners with a mortgage pay a median of $4,000 a month, and median gross rent is $1,951. The county averages 2,332 people per square mile across 430.72 square miles of land, and 34.8 percent of residents age five and over speak a language other than English at home. Because the county mixes dense cities with large-lot suburbs, a median value tells you little about your own street. Look at recent nearby sales.

Corporate headquarters in the county include IBM, Mastercard, PepsiCo and Regeneron, according to the county's Wikipedia entry, and the Bronx River Parkway, completed in 1925, was the first modern multi-lane limited-access road in North America.

What should I check before selling a Westchester County house with tax due?

Request a payoff from the city or town receiver of taxes, since that office holds the combined county, local and school figures. Then work through a short list.

  • Find out which installments are paid and which are open, including school tax.
  • Ask whether the bill is on a lien list and whether a sale or redemption deadline is coming.
  • Ask for the exact payoff date that interest runs to.
  • Check whether a Small Claim Assessment Review or a certiorari case is pending on the parcel.
  • Confirm the owner name and mailing address on the assessment roll.

A cash buyer can close with these balances open, and the title company pays them from your proceeds at the table. What you net depends on the payoff amounts, so get them in writing.

Frequently asked questions

Do I pay Westchester County property tax to the county?

No. You pay your city or town, which also bills the county's share. The county's Tax Commission asks owners not to mail property tax checks to the county.

Does Westchester County sell tax liens?

No. The County Finance Department says it does not run delinquent tax lien sales. The city or town where the property sits conducts them.

Where do I send paperwork for a Westchester small claims refund?

Your municipality sends it to County Finance, Attn: SCAR Processing, 148 Martine Avenue, Suite 724, White Plains, NY 10601. You do not mail the county form yourself.

How can I find a Westchester city's tax dates?

Use the county's chart of property tax payment dates, which lists the last day to pay without penalty for each municipality. Yonkers dates vary with the City Council's levy date, so confirm with the city's tax office.

Who can answer questions about Westchester equalization rates?

The County Tax Commission in White Plains, phone 914-995-4325. It publishes equalization tables and historical rates, and its page invites questions about county property taxes and exemptions.

Who collects property tax in Rockland County?

A town receiver collects the first payment, and the County Department of Finance takes over any unpaid balance on April 1. Rockland County has five towns, so the receiver you pay in January depends on whether your house is in Clarkstown, Haverstraw, Orangetown, Ramapo or Stony Point.

The county seat is New City, and eighteen incorporated villages sit inside the towns. That mix explains why two neighbors can have different assessors and different local bills even though the county collection rules are the same.

The Department of Finance sits at 50 Sanatorium Road, Building A, 8th Floor, Pomona, NY 10970. The main number is (845) 364-3870, and the tax unit answers at (845) 364-3877. Office hours are Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

The quarterly payment plan

Owners can split the combined county and town tax into four payments with a 5 percent service charge, and the first of the four is due January 15 to the town receiver. The second, third and fourth payments go to the Commissioner of Finance.

The plan comes with firm consequences:

  • Miss any quarterly payment and the whole unpaid balance becomes due at once.
  • A 5 percent penalty is added to that balance, with interest of 1 percent per month until it is paid.
  • Only certain towns offer the plan, so ask your receiver whether yours does before you count on it.

An owner who skips the plan and has not paid the receiver by March 31 sees the account transferred to the Commissioner of Finance on April 1. From that date the payment goes to Pomona, not to the town hall.

Collection dates

The county's dates cluster in the first half of the year, with the January 15 receiver payment and the April 1 transfer to the Commissioner doing most of the work for a delinquent account.

Quarterly payments two through four are made to the Commissioner of Finance and may be paid through the county's online system. Call (845) 364-3877 or (845) 364-3878 for details of an installment agreement, which can be paid off in full at any time.

How do I pay overdue Rockland County tax?

Pay online with an electronic check, which costs nothing, or by credit card, which carries a 3 percent fee. You can also mail a check, certified funds or a money order payable to the Commissioner of Finance.

The mailing address is Commissioner of Finance, 50 Sanatorium Road, Bldg. A, 8th Floor, Pomona, NY 10970. Tax searches and duplicate receipts are available by calling the tax office, and you should call for an updated payoff figure when an amount is in question. Because interest keeps running at 1 percent a month on a defaulted balance, a figure from last month can be wrong.

Foreclosure and county auctions

Yes, the county forecloses on unpaid property tax. Its own example is that taxes for 2010 would be subject to foreclosure around June 2012, about two years after the tax year. The Department of Finance also runs auctions of county-owned property acquired through foreclosure. Watch the finance page for the next auction notice.

New York law gives a delinquent tax lien a two-year redemption period, with a district allowed to extend it for homes, under RPTL section 1110. The practical message for a Rockland owner is to act while the account is still with the town receiver or in its first year with the county, and call the tax unit about an installment agreement before the account ages further.

Who sets and reviews the assessment on a Rockland house?

The assessor in your own town does, not the county. Owners with an assessment question should contact the assessor's office in the town where they live.

That means a Haverstraw owner and an Orangetown owner file with different offices and may face different dates. Ask your town assessor for its grievance date and exemption deadlines. For a sale, pull the current assessed value and any exemptions from the town, because the county only collects what the town rolls produce.

Rockland County's Department of Finance does not set values. Its role is the money side: collection of delinquent taxes, tax searches, and the auction of properties the county has acquired.

What happens to the tax bill when I sell

The title company asks the county or the town receiver for a tax search and pays any open balance from the sale proceeds at closing, so owing tax does not prevent a sale. The balance simply reduces what you take home.

Two steps help a closing go smoothly. First, find out whether the account is still with the town receiver or has gone to the Commissioner of Finance, since that decides which office issues the payoff. Second, if you were using the quarterly plan, ask for the remaining balance with the 5 percent service charge included, because the plan's charges attach to the account.

A buyer paying cash for a house as it stands still needs those figures, and having a written payoff on hand before the contract is signed keeps the closing date from slipping.

Which office you call depends on the calendar. From the start of the year to March 31, the town receiver is your contact, and the first quarterly payment is due January 15. From April 1, the Commissioner of Finance in Pomona holds any unpaid account, and May 1 is when installment agreements open for current-year taxes. Have your parcel details and last bill in front of you when you call, and ask whether the account is on the quarterly plan, because the 5 percent service charge and any penalty travel with the account into the closing.

If you are behind, do not wait for a foreclosure notice. Interest of 1 percent a month keeps building, and a sale that pays everything at closing is a cleaner exit than letting the account age toward the two-year point.

Rockland housing snapshot

Rockland County is expensive and mostly owner-occupied, at 67.9 percent, with a median home value of $596,900. The July 2025 population estimate is 357,397, up 5.6 percent from the April 2020 base. There are 109,999 housing units and 103,879 households, averaging 3.22 people each. Median gross rent is $1,901, and median monthly owner costs with a mortgage are $3,641.

Frequently asked questions

Which office do I call about Rockland County property tax?

The Department of Finance tax unit at (845) 364-3877, or the main line at (845) 364-3870. For a value or exemption question, call the assessor in your own town.

When does Rockland turn unpaid tax over to the county?

April 1. If the receiver has not been paid by March 31, the account goes to the Commissioner of Finance on April 1.

Is there a fee for paying Rockland tax by card?

Yes, 3 percent for a credit card. An electronic check through the same online system has no charge.

What happens if I miss a quarterly payment in Rockland?

The whole unpaid balance comes due immediately with a 5 percent penalty and 1 percent interest per month. Call the tax unit before that happens to ask about an installment agreement.

Can I sell my Rockland house with unpaid tax?

Yes. The balance is paid out of your proceeds at closing, and the Commissioner of Finance or the town receiver supplies the payoff figure.

Orange County in brief

Orange County sits in the Hudson Valley with Goshen as its seat. Its three cities are Middletown, Newburgh and Port Jervis, and the rest is split into 20 towns with a scattering of villages. About 417,669 people lived here as of July 2025, up 4.1% since 2020, in 138,608 households. The median owner-occupied home is worth $387,900 and median gross rent is $1,680.

Who collects property tax in Orange County?

Town, county and special district bills are mailed by the town and paid to the town collector without penalty during the collection window. Delinquent amounts and penalties go to the county Department of Finance, now on the third floor of the County Building at 255 Main Street in Goshen. The county's page lists 845-291-2480 for questions.

Three cities are carved out. The county does not collect or enforce taxes inside Middletown, Newburgh or Port Jervis, so owners there deal with the city directly. Properties outside those cities but inside the Middletown, Newburgh or Port Jervis school districts pay current school tax to the district and only pay the county once the bill turns delinquent.

VillageJune through October (a few villages start earlier)Village

Delinquent school tax from outside-city parcels reaches the county in March for Middletown, April for Newburgh and November for Port Jervis, on the county's calendar.

The tax foreclosure auction

The county takes possession of parcels for unpaid tax through a foreclosure once a year, and the parcels are then offered at a public auction. A booklet with general information and the list of parcels is available from the Real Property Tax office before the sale.

Parcels that do not sell go onto a leftover list that used to be open for bids each month, but that deed sale process is paused because of recent changes to New York's Real Property Tax Law. Bids on the leftover list require official bank checks or money orders and a 10 percent deposit, not cash.

The county also posts surplus and non-surplus reports for the 2024 and 2025 auctions and the 2025 leftover list, which follow the state's Article 11 changes. Anyone claiming surplus funds should consult an attorney. A seller who is behind should ask Finance how far the foreclosure has gone before choosing between paying, selling and waiting.

Grievances and state relief

Assessments in Orange County are set by the town or city assessor, so complaints go to the local board of assessment review. State law opens those hearings on the fourth Tuesday of May unless a local law sets another date, so check the date with your assessor. If the board leaves the value unchanged, Small Claims Assessment Review is the lower-cost court route for most homeowners, and a tax certiorari case in State Supreme Court is the route that calls for an attorney.

The county's parcel search lets you look up owner, assessed values, tax maps, photos and comparable sales for any parcel, and it is useful before a grievance and before pricing a sale. For state relief, the STAR credit is registered through the State Tax Department's Homeowner Benefit Portal, and a seller should close that registration at the sale.

What changes if my house is inside a village or a city?

A village adds its own bill. Owners in a village pay current and late village tax to the village itself up to October 31, so a village balance is not something to settle at the county office. Most villages mail bills in June, while South Blooming Grove and the Village of Kiryas mail in January and Cornwall-on-Hudson and Washingtonville mail in March.

City owners have their own offices. The county's collection page lists the City of Middletown at 845-346-4150, the City of Newburgh at 845-569-7330 and the City of Port Jervis at 845-858-4014. Each city's school district sets its own dates as well, and the three districts publish their own phone numbers for tax questions.

For a sale, this means several balances may sit on one house, such as town and county, village or city, and school. Ask the closing attorney to request each payoff separately, and match every figure to the day of closing so nothing is left behind on the next bill.

Selling with tax due

Work out which collector holds the balance. In a town, current bills sit with the town collector until the window closes and then move to the county Department of Finance. In Middletown, Newburgh or Port Jervis, call the city.

  • Ask for a payoff figure in writing, with the date it is good through.
  • Ask whether foreclosure has started on the parcel.
  • Give the figure to your attorney so it is paid at closing.
  • Close your STAR registration if you receive that benefit.

A buyer paying cash can purchase the house as it is, with the lien, any repairs and any tenants. Whichever route you pick, the payoff is deducted from what you receive, so knowing it before you accept an offer tells you what you will actually take home.

From unpaid bill to closing, step by step

The order of events in Orange County is predictable, which helps if you are deciding how fast to move.

  1. The town collector takes the bill without penalty during the window, which for county and town tax runs January through March.
  2. Once the window closes, unpaid county and town tax moves to the Department of Finance in Goshen along with penalties.
  3. If it stays unpaid, the county can foreclose, and parcels it takes are offered at the yearly public auction.
  4. Parcels that do not sell land on the leftover list.

A sale at any point before foreclosure is complete lets the payoff come out of your proceeds. Bring the latest bill, your parcel number, and any notice from the county or city when you call for the figure. Ask the person on the phone to put it in writing, and confirm the date it is good through, because interest and penalties keep running on a delinquent balance.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay delinquent property tax in Orange County, NY?

Delinquent county and town tax goes to the Orange County Department of Finance, on the third floor of the County Building at 255 Main Street in Goshen. The number on the county's pages is 845-291-2480. Inside the cities of Middletown, Newburgh and Port Jervis the county does not collect, so call the city.

When are Orange County property tax bills collected?

Collection periods vary by town, but county and town tax is generally collected January through March, school tax September through November and village tax June through October. Your own bill states the dates that apply, and your municipality's collector can confirm them.

Is the Orange County tax auction happening now?

The county's auction page currently shows no tax delinquency auctions scheduled. It also says the leftover list deed sale is paused because of changes to state tax law. Sign up for the page's email alerts or ask the Real Property Tax office for updates.

What can I do if I think my Orange County assessment is too high?

File a complaint with your town or city board of assessment review, which meets starting the fourth Tuesday in May unless a local law sets another date. If that fails, Small Claims Assessment Review is open to most homeowners. Call your assessor first, since an informal talk can fix errors.

Can I sell my house in Orange County before foreclosure?

Yes. The county can only auction a parcel once foreclosure is complete, and a sale that pays the full tax lien at closing clears the debt. Ask Finance for a written payoff and which stage your parcel has reached, and do not wait for an auction notice.

Which Erie County office handles what

Erie County divides the work. City and town assessors set values, town tax receivers collect current bills, and the county's Real Property Tax Services (RPTS) office handles delinquent county tax and foreclosure.

The county's Pay Your Taxes page takes current City of Buffalo county property taxes and delinquent Erie County taxes for any town or city in the county, and lets you look up what is owed. If you live outside Buffalo, current tax goes to your town receiver.

How Erie County forecloses on unpaid tax

The county can foreclose on a tax lien once it has gone unpaid for two or more years, using a numbered in rem proceeding. In Rem 173 covered liens through tax year 2022, and the county filed its List of Delinquent Taxes with the County Clerk on September 9, 2025. A statutory foreclosure fee of $500 had to accompany the unpaid liens. A later round, In Rem 174, began on May 5, 2026. Call RPTS for the status of that round and the next sale schedule.

  • Pay with cash, certified check, bank check or money order. Personal checks are not accepted.
  • Interest is applied on the first day of each month, so the payoff figure changes monthly.
  • Paying old liens does not stop later years from becoming eligible, so open 2023, 2024 and 2025 county taxes keep accruing interest and fees.
  • Payment plans may be available for certain residential, owner-occupied property, case by case.

Scammers target owners in foreclosure. Neither the county nor its attorneys will ask for gift cards, cryptocurrency, wire transfers or online banking logins. Free help is available from the state Attorney General's Homeowner Protection Program at 1-855-HOME-456.

Housing and taxes across the county

About 946,741 people live in Erie County, and roughly 65.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied. The typical home is valued at $233,800 and the typical rent is $1,090. The county has 16 villages, including Williamsville, Hamburg, Kenmore, East Aurora and Orchard Park, and school districts range from Buffalo City to small central districts such as Holland and Akron. Tax bills therefore vary by town, village and district.

Interest is added on the first of every month, so mark the redemption date in each in rem notice on a calendar. Notices also go to mortgage holders and others with an interest in the parcel, and those recipients are advised to speak with an attorney to protect their position.

Does STAR work differently in Buffalo?

Yes. STAR applies only to school district taxes, with five cities as exceptions: New York, Buffalo, Rochester, Yonkers and Syracuse. In those cities the benefit is applied partly to city taxes and partly to school taxes. A Buffalo homeowner and a Lancaster homeowner can therefore see the benefit land on different lines of the bill.

The credit comes as a check or direct deposit. The older STAR exemption on the bill continues only for owners who have held it since 2015 on the same home, and new homeowners register for the credit. Basic STAR has a $500,000 income limit, and Enhanced STAR for owners aged 65 and over needs income of $110,750 or less for the 2026-2027 school year.

Selling with taxes owed

Work out which level of government you owe, because the answers come from different offices. County liens near foreclosure sit with RPTS. Current town and school tax sits with the town receiver. The RPTS online system shows county amounts, and the tax line at (716) 858-8333 can give an exact payoff.

  1. Look up the parcel on the county's payment site and note every open year, since foreclosure eligibility turns on liens at least two years old.
  2. If the parcel appears on a foreclosure list, find the last day of redemption and the answer deadline in the notice you received.
  3. Call RPTS to ask whether a payment plan is possible for an owner-occupied home.
  4. Pass the payoff figures to your closing attorney so the lien is cleared at or before closing.

A cash buyer can close quickly and pay the lien from proceeds, which stops further monthly interest. Collect the figure in writing and ask that it be good through your closing date.

Reading an in rem notice

A notice is not a bill, and it is worth reading line by line. It states the last day to redeem and the deadline to answer, and it names the lien years covered. Because interest is added on the first day of each month, the amount shown is only good until that date, so ask RPTS for an updated payoff before you send anything. The foreclosure fee goes in a separate check, and payment must be by cash, certified check, bank check or money order.

Mortgage holders and others with an interest in the parcel receive the same notice. If you own the house with someone else or have a lender, find out who is responding so that no one assumes the other is handling it.

What a cash sale can do for a lien

Erie County owners often come to a sale because tax liens, interest and fees have piled up over several years. A cash purchase can pay the county from the proceeds at closing, which stops monthly interest and keeps later years from becoming eligible for foreclosure. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to repair anything first, and you owe nothing if you decline an offer.

The practical steps are short. Ask RPTS for the payoff, ask your town receiver about any current bill, and share both figures with us. We include them in the written offer, and the title company pays each office when the deed is recorded. If a payment plan is available for your owner-occupied home, you can compare it with a sale and choose the path that suits you.

Surplus money after an auction

If a house has already been sold at auction, the former owner may be owed surplus money. The claimant files a Notice of Claim in the County Clerk's Office and starts a legal proceeding on notice to others with an interest. A lawyer is not required. A judge decides who receives what. The County Comptroller, at (716) 858-8400, holds the surplus.

Who helps owners facing foreclosure

Free counseling and legal help are available. The New York State Attorney General's Homeowner Protection Program, at 1-855-HOME-456, connects owners to housing counselors and attorneys at no charge. Avoid anyone who charges a fee to guarantee foreclosure relief. If you have received an in rem notice, read the redemption and answer deadlines first, then call RPTS before doing anything else.

How long must an Erie County tax lien go unpaid before foreclosure?

Two years or more. In Rem 173 covered liens through tax year 2022.

How much is the Erie County foreclosure fee?

$500, paid on top of the unpaid liens and interest. It should be issued as a separate check.

Can I pay Erie County delinquent tax online?

Yes. The county's online system accepts delinquent Erie County property taxes for any town or city in the county, and current county tax for the City of Buffalo. Current bills elsewhere go to the town receiver.

Is there an Erie County foreclosure auction coming up?

Call RPTS at (716) 858-8333 for the next sale schedule and the status of In Rem 174.

Where to pay and ask about property tax in Monroe County

In Monroe County, the Treasury Division of the Department of Finance collects fees and taxes at the County Office Building, Room B2, 39 W. Main Street in Rochester, phone 585 753-1200. Your town or city tax receiver and your assessor are separate offices, and the county publishes a contact table for both.

Monroe County lies on the southern shore of Lake Ontario, with Rochester as county seat and largest city. The county's table lists twenty town offices, from Brighton and Chili to Webster and Wheatland, plus the City of Rochester. Each assessor sets values for its own roll, so a house in Pittsford and a house in Greece are assessed by different offices on the same county calendar.

In the City of Rochester, the assessor and the tax receiver both work from City Hall, Room 101-A, at 30 Church Street. Suburban owners deal with their town hall instead, and a few towns share an assessor: the same assessor covers Mendon and East Rochester, and another covers Gates and Ogden.

  • Pay or look up a bill through the county's Real Property Portal, linked from the Treasury page.
  • Ask your town assessor about value, exemptions and Grievance Day.
  • Ask the town or city tax receiver about a bill that has not arrived.

When Monroe County tax bills are due

The combined town and county bill is mailed by December 31 and is due in full on February 10, or in four installments on February 10, February 28, March 30 and April 30. School bills are mailed by August 31 and are due October 1, with three installment dates of September 15, October 15 and November 15.

Once the third school installment date, November 15, goes by, the balance counts as unpaid school tax. Any unpaid school balance, plus penalty and interest, is re-levied onto the next combined town and county bill. In other words, a school balance you ignore in the fall comes back on the January bill under the county's name.

Owners aged 65 or older, or with a disability, who live in a one- to three-family home can name a trusted adult to receive duplicate bills and unpaid-tax notices. The application deadline is November 1 each year. This helps a seller who is older or ill and wants a relative to catch notices, so nothing is missed while a house is on the market.

If you pay in installments, mark all four dates early in the year and keep the receipts. A seller who closes in the spring should ask the town or city receiver which installments are posted, so that the payoff on the closing statement matches the county's records.

What happens when Monroe County property tax goes unpaid?

Assessment and grievance dates

Town property is valued as of July 1 and taxable status is March 1, the date exemption applications must be filed. The tentative roll is filed May 1, Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday of May, and the final roll is signed July 1.

For 2027 the fourth Tuesday of May is May 25, but confirm with your local assessor. The City of Rochester runs on a different calendar: its valuation date and taxable status date are both February 1, and its tentative roll comes March 1. A seller in Rochester therefore has an earlier window to challenge value than a seller in a suburban town.

Monroe County also posts its tax rate tables online, including 2026 town and county rates, 2025-26 school rates, 2025 village rates and 2026 special district rates. If you suspect you pay too much, compare your rate lines before you decide whether an appeal is worth the effort.

Monroe County is the most urban part of upstate here, with 750,506 residents in the July 2025 estimate and 342,061 housing units on about 657 square miles of land. Owners occupy 63.7% of homes, so rental properties are a large share of the market. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $213,700, median household income is $76,382, and median gross rent is $1,173. The mean commute is 19.9 minutes.

The county-wide median hides wide differences between lakeshore suburbs and Rochester neighborhoods, so check your own parcel's assessment and tax rate lines instead of leaning on the average. A written payoff from the Treasury office gives a buyer or title company a firm number to work from.

How do I sell a Monroe County house with tax owed?

Get a current payoff from the Treasury office, then decide whether to pay it, set up a payment plan or sell before the August 15 publication. County staff will try to negotiate a plan during the whole process, and housing counseling agencies such as the Urban League of Rochester and The Housing Council are named on the county's page.

If a plan is not workable, selling can clear the balance from proceeds. A buyer who pays cash and takes the home in its present condition can shorten the timeline, which helps when a publication date or auction schedule is near.

  1. Ask Treasury for a payoff figure for the parcel.
  2. Ask about a payment plan, which protects a parcel while payments stay current.
  3. Compare closing dates with August 15 and the September auction month.

When you call 585 753-1200, have the tax account or parcel number ready and say whether a lender escrows your taxes. Ask for the payoff in writing and for the date through which it is good, since penalty and interest keep adding up. February 10 is the due date for full payment, with installments due February 10, February 28, March 30 and April 30. The bill is mailed by December 31 to your lender if you escrow, or to you directly.

What is Grievance Day in Monroe County?

It is the fourth Tuesday in May in the towns, which is May 25, 2027. The Board of Assessment Review meets then, and it is the last day to file a formal complaint against a tentative assessment. Confirm locally.

Does Monroe County have a payment plan for back taxes?

Yes. County Treasury staff try to negotiate a plan with owners, and a signed plan with no missed payments keeps a parcel out of foreclosure. Call 585 753-1200 to ask.

When does Monroe County list delinquent properties?

By law the list of lands with unpaid taxes is published on August 15, and the county declares taxes delinquent on August 20. A second publication follows if the balance stays unpaid into the next year.

What happens to unpaid school tax in Monroe County?

The unpaid school balance, with penalty and interest, is re-levied as a county tax on the next combined town and county bill. That is why it can show up again in January.

A county tax not paid by March 31 and a school or village tax not paid by November 1 are treated as delinquent by the county. Ask RPTS for the exact total on your parcel.

How long can I redeem a parcel with a delinquent tax lien?

The default redemption period is two years from the lien date under Real Property Tax Law section 1110. A tax district can extend it for residential and farm property or shorten it to one year for vacant and abandoned homes. Ask the county which period applies to your parcel.

When is the Onondaga County tax auction?

The county holds its real property tax auction once a year in October, online, and it starts listing parcels in September. For the current list, use the RPTS auction page, since the parcels change every year.

Who bills and collects property tax in Oswego County?

The county does not run a single bill. Oswego County describes four separate bills: county and town, city, village and school. Local tax collectors take the first payments. Afterward, the County Treasurer is the enforcing officer for unpaid taxes everywhere except the City of Fulton, where the Fulton City Chamberlain enforces city, county and school tax.

The county's Real Property Tax Services department, at 46 E. Bridge Street in Oswego, keeps tax maps and the assessment software. It does not set assessments, collect taxes or keep payment receipts. The county's general line is 800-596-3200.

  • Assessments and exemption approvals: your town or city assessor.
  • Payments during the first collection window: the local tax collector named on your bill.

Tax dates and interest charges

A county and town bill is due by January 31 without interest, with local collection running to March 31, and unpaid balances are returned to the county in mid-April. Interest is simple during local collection. A county or town bill adds 1 percent after 30 days and 1 percent for each further month, a village bill adds 5 percent after 30 days, and a school bill adds 2 percent.

County and town bills may be paid in two equal installments unless an escrow account pays them. The first goes to the local collector by March 31, and the second goes to the County Treasurer by June 30 with interest on the remaining balance.

A bill that never arrives does not cancel the tax. Property taxes are levied against the land and buildings, so a sale transfers the problem to the buyer unless the balance is paid at closing.

How does an Oswego County tax foreclosure work?

Every property tax becomes a lien on the property and stays one until paid. The county starts Article 11 foreclosure on taxes that remain unpaid two years after they were issued, or four years for agricultural land. It holds two foreclosures each year in that way, and everything it forecloses on is sold together at one auction.

State law lets an owner redeem a delinquent lien by paying the enforcing officer before the redemption period ends, which is two years after the lien date unless the tax district sets another period (section 1110). Ask the Treasurer which date applies to your parcel.

The auction rules are strict. Buyers must have photo identification and a Social Security number, must not owe delinquent Oswego County tax, and must pay a buyer's premium and administrative fee, with any bid under $1,000 paid in full that day. The county sells tax-foreclosed houses as-is, does not warrant title, and gives the winner a tax deed. A former owner who is still behind has far more choices before the auction than on the day of it.

How do I sell an Oswego County house with taxes behind?

  • Ask whether village or school balances have been re-levied onto the January county bill.

A deed must be filed to move title in New York, and the county advises speaking to a lawyer about the type of deed. A sale that closes before the foreclosure date can pay the tax from the proceeds and clear the lien.

Before you list

A short checklist keeps surprises out of the contract period. Pull the parcel in the Real Property Database and look at the billed amounts and delinquent status. Ask your town or city assessor which exemptions you hold and whether any end at the sale, and keep copies of every bill you have paid this year. Call the Treasurer, or the Fulton Chamberlain, about the payoff and any payment plan. Confirm with your attorney what kind of deed the sale needs.

If the house is tax-foreclosed it sells as-is with no title warranty, so a former owner who still has the right to redeem is usually better off selling or paying before that point. A cash buyer takes the house as it stands and skips repair requests, which can matter when the clock is running on a foreclosure date. Either way, the payoff comes out of your proceeds at closing.

Timing matters most around the January 1 county and town bill. Local collection runs until March 31, and unpaid balances come back to the county in mid-April, after which the County Treasurer is your contact. Which Jefferson County offices deal with property tax?

Jefferson County splits the job among town and city assessors, local tax collectors and two county offices in Watertown. How to pay a Jefferson County tax bill

Start with a call to the Treasurer at 315-785-3055 or an email to treasurer@jeffersoncountyny.gov. Verify the amount and the collector before you pay, because the office rejects and returns a payment sent for the wrong amount or to the wrong collector.

  • By mail or in person at 175 Arsenal Street, Watertown, NY 13601, with checks payable to the Jefferson County Treasurer.
  • Online, using the tax map number or 911 address plus the installment number as the ID. Cards carry a 3.0% fee plus 69 cents, and American Express is not taken.
  • Village and school bills go to the village or the school district named on the bill.

Treasurer hours are 9 am to 5 pm from September 1 through June 30, with collections until 4:45 pm. In July and August the hours are 8:30 am to 4 pm. The date full town and county payments open changes from year to year, so ask when the current year's collection begins.

Challenging an assessment in Jefferson County

File Form RP-524 with the assessor or Board of Assessment Review in your town or city by Grievance Day. In most New York communities that day is the fourth Tuesday in May, which is May 25 in 2027, but confirm it with your local assessor or municipal clerk.

Filing is free and needs no lawyer. Only the assessment on the current tentative roll can be grieved. If the board turns you down, an owner-occupied home qualifies for Small Claims Assessment Review at $30, started within 30 days after the final roll is filed. Villages that assess their own property keep separate dates, usually in February, so a village homeowner may have two assessments to check.

The county office can help local assessors on valuations, small claims hearings and rolls, while the local board hears the grievance itself. Call Real Property Tax Services at 315-785-3074 with questions about a parcel's tax map or address.

What happens when Jefferson County taxes go unpaid?

The county can foreclose, and its FAQ describes how to stop it. A parcel is saved by paying every delinquent tax, interest, penalty and fee before the redemption date, or by signing an installment agreement for owners who qualify.

  • An installment agreement requires 25% down on all delinquent amounts for the owner's county properties outside Watertown, then eight roughly equal quarterly payments over two years, with new taxes paid in full and on time.
  • An owner is eligible once at least 30 days late, but not after defaulting on an earlier agreement or losing property to foreclosure within three years.
  • State law requires redeeming the newest taxes first, so paying only the oldest year does not remove a parcel from the list.
  • Deadlines are firm, and extensions are not possible. Only a majority vote of the County Legislature can waive penalties and interest.

Once the county takes title at foreclosure, the former owner's interest ends. The county generally offers the property at its annual tax auction, selling as-is by quitclaim deed, and an auction buyer takes on the school and village tax for the auction year. Buyers may face unpaid water, sewer or utility bills, easements and zoning limits, and the county gives no guarantee about boundaries or size. For a seller, that is a reason to resolve the tax before the parcel reaches the auction list.

What to do about Jefferson County tax before selling

Tax liens follow the property, so a buyer inherits the bill even if the seller never mentions it. A seller with delinquent tax should get a written payoff from the Treasurer and settle it from the sale proceeds, or sell before the foreclosure date.

  2. Ask the Treasurer for the delinquent balance with interest through the closing date.
  3. Tell the title company about any installment agreement so the remaining balance is paid off at closing.

A third party who pays your tax does not gain the house, since the old tax sale certificate practice ended years ago. An owner who inherited a home in Le Ray, Clayton or Adams and fell behind does not have to wait for an auction. A cash sale can bring the tax current in one closing. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff letter that runs through your expected closing date, since interest keeps accruing until the day the money arrives.

Timing helps here. A parcel moves from a local collector to the Treasurer once it turns delinquent, and from the Treasurer to the foreclosure process after that. The earlier you act, the fewer offices you have to deal with at once. Bring the tax map number or 911 address to every call, since both the online payment system and the staff look parcels up that way. If the house is in the City of Watertown, remember that the county's collection work does not cover it, so call the city instead.

Jefferson County housing at a glance

Jefferson County sits on New York's northern border where the St. Lawrence River leaves Lake Ontario. Watertown is the county seat, and Le Ray is the largest town, with a 2020 count of 25,574. The Fort Drum base is in the county. Villages include Carthage, West Carthage, Clayton, Adams, Sackets Harbor, Alexandria Bay and Cape Vincent.

The county has an estimated 111,540 residents as of July 2025, down 4.4% from the 2020 base, across 62,392 housing units. Homeowners occupy 54.7% of units, the median owner-occupied value is $188,200, and median rent is $1,213. Median household income is $66,301. Summer tourism lifts the population noticeably, so a listing that sits through the winter can look different in July.

The County Treasurer collects delinquent village, school, town and county real property tax, except in the City of Watertown. The office is at 175 Arsenal Street in Watertown, 315-785-3055.

Can I get an extension on Jefferson County foreclosure deadlines?

No. All deadlines are firm. The only ways to save the property are paying everything owed before the redemption date or entering an installment agreement.

How does a Jefferson County installment agreement work?

You pay 25% of all delinquent taxes, interest, fees and penalties up front, then eight roughly equal quarterly payments over two years. You must also keep all new taxes current.

When is Grievance Day in Jefferson County?

In most New York communities it is the fourth Tuesday in May, which is May 25 in 2027. Confirm the date with your town or city assessor, since villages and some cities differ.

Does paying someone else's delinquent tax give me their Jefferson County property?

No. The sale of tax certificates ended years ago, and ownership stays with the owner of record no matter who pays.

Who bills and collects property tax in Wayne County, NY?

The town tax collector sends and collects your combined town and county bill, and the Wayne County Treasurer in Lyons takes over a bill that is still unpaid after March. Wayne County has no cities. It has 15 towns and seven villages on the south shore of Lake Ontario, between Rochester and Syracuse, and Lyons is the county seat.

The county's Real Property Tax Services Agency works behind the scenes. Its 2024 annual report says it produces the assessment rolls, tax rolls and tax bills for the towns, villages and school districts, keeps the tax maps, investigates correction-of-error requests, divides the county levy among the assessing jurisdictions and calculates tax rates. It also supplies bills to 22 school districts, some of which lie outside the county.

  • Town tax collector: current Town and County bill, January through March.
  • County Treasurer, P.O. Box 8, Lyons, NY 14489, phone 315-946-7441: delinquent bills, installment agreements and the foreclosure auction.
  • Town assessor: value, exemption forms and ownership changes.
  • Real Property Tax Service page on the county site: assessment rolls, tax maps, rate documents and a parcel viewer.

When are Wayne County property taxes due?

Town and County bills are issued by each town around January 1 and are payable to the town collector in January, February and March. The county's Taxpayers Guide sets the cost of waiting: nothing extra in January, 1 percent added in February and 2 percent added in March.

The tax year runs from January 1 to December 31. The Treasurer's FAQ says an owner can pay current taxes in two payments. The first falls due by the end of the penalty-free period, and the second is due in February or March with interest added. The same FAQ warns that a buyer who closed after March 1 will not receive a bill until the next billing cycle, and that the owner remains responsible for paying on time even when no bill arrives.

Rural fire, rural light and rural water or sewer charges can appear on a bill as special assessments, so a parcel in the countryside may carry lines that a village lot does not. Your bill is the taxable assessment multiplied by the rate, plus those special charges.

What happens when Wayne County taxes go unpaid?

On April 1 the town bill is treated as delinquent and goes to the County Treasurer, and the county can foreclose when taxes stay unpaid for two years. The Taxpayers Guide describes a ladder of added costs once the Treasurer holds the bill.

  • April 1: the bill moves to the Treasurer, and the guide mentions a 25 percent penalty at transfer.
  • After receipt: the guide lists a 5 percent penalty and 1 percent interest for each month the tax stays delinquent.
  • September of the second year: an enforcement fee of $450 or more is added, and the parcel is advertised in local papers for three non-consecutive weeks.
  • March, tentatively: the last chance to redeem before foreclosure, followed by a public auction of unpaid parcels in June.

The Treasurer's FAQ describes a payment program for eligible owners. It is available for delinquent taxes after June 1, runs up to 24 months and needs a down payment of at least 10 percent. Call the office before any step above, because the payoff changes every month.

State law sets the outer frame. Under RPTL 1110 a delinquent lien can be redeemed by paying the amount due plus legal charges before the redemption period ends, normally two years after the lien date. The county's 2024 report adds that a 2024 change to Article 11 now returns surplus proceeds of a tax sale to the former owner. The county held its 2024 online auction from May 30 to June 19 with about 15 parcels, and the Treasurer's office handles sales from now on.

Anything still open on November 1 gets relevied. For a seller this matters because a January bill that looks too large may contain last fall's school or village balance. Ask the Treasurer or your town collector whether any relevy appears, and check the county site for the date a bill was paid.

How is a Wayne County assessment set and challenged?

Your town assessor sets your assessment, and a local Board of Assessment Review hears complaints. According to the county's 2024 report, every town has a five-member board except Ontario, Savannah and Sodus, and Sodus moved to three members during 2024. The report does not give a grievance date, so ask your town assessor when filing closes.

Owners of one-, two- and three-family owner-occupied homes can go on to a Small Claims Assessment Review hearing. Anyone may file a certiorari petition in Supreme Court. The county's policy, adopted by the Board of Supervisors in 1995, is that it learns of a case only when the assessed value reaches $1,000,000, the threshold for county participation. Clerical errors and similar mistakes can be corrected under RPTL 550 to 559.

Equalization rates show how far each town's roll sits from full market value. The county keeps pointing to 100 percent as the goal because it means fewer correction, small claims and certiorari filings. What does farm land mean for a Wayne County tax bill?

Working orchards and fields can qualify for an agricultural assessment, and Wayne County has a lot of it. The county's report says about 174,632 of 295,113 acres in the agricultural district receive an exemption under Article 25-AA, and it calls Wayne the largest apple-producing county in New York, based on the 2022 Census of Agriculture.

If you sell a house with acreage, ask the town assessor whether the land carries an agricultural assessment and what a change of use would do. The report credits the Lake Ontario shore climate for the fruit industry. A buyer who plans to stop farming should hear about any change in assessment before the contract is signed.

Wayne County had an estimated 91,250 residents in July 2025 and 43,064 housing units. Owners occupy 79.9 percent of homes, which is a high share, and the median owner-occupied home is valued at $170,000 for 2020 to 2024.

Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,541, against $666 without one. Median gross rent is $938, median household income is $74,506, and the county covers 603.83 square miles of land. Largest town by population is Arcadia, and Newark is the biggest village. These are countywide medians, so a lake-view property in Sodus Point and a village house in Clyde can differ widely.

What should I do before selling a Wayne County house with tax due?

Get a written payoff from the right office for each layer of tax, because the town collector, the Treasurer, the village and the school district each hold different pieces. A short list keeps the closing on schedule.

  • Call the Treasurer at 315-946-7441 if any bill went past April 1, and ask for the figure including penalties, interest and any enforcement fee.
  • Ask whether village or school balances were relevied onto the January bill.
  • Confirm with the town assessor that the owner name and any farm or senior exemption are correct.

Two years of unpaid taxes. The Treasurer's FAQ says the county can foreclose when taxes remain unpaid for two years, and the Taxpayers Guide places the public auction in June and the tentative last redemption date in March.

You will not get a bill until the next billing cycle, but you are still responsible for paying on time. Ask the town tax collector for the amount before the penalty-free period ends.

Town, city and county bills go out on January 1, village bills on June 1 and school bills on September 1. A missed bill does not excuse the tax, because interest and penalties are not waived when a bill never arrived. Call the collector if nothing shows up in the first week.

Interest on unpaid town and county tax starts February 1 at 1% per month. After April 30 the unpaid balance returns to the Treasurer, who adds a 5% county return penalty on the original tax while the 1% monthly interest keeps running. A town may also add a notice fee. The Treasurer mails updated amounts due from time to time, so a payoff figure you were quoted in spring can change by closing.

School tax follows its own path. Each year the school tax collector sends the Treasurer a list of unpaid school taxes on or before November 15, and that balance then joins the county's delinquent file.

If the assessor does not move, take your evidence to the town's independent Board of Assessment Review on Grievance Day. Ask the Treasurer for a written payoff before you accept any offer, because penalties, the $250 lien-search fee and the $100 posting fee change the total. Then pick a closing date that falls ahead of the next county step, such as the July advertisement or the September auction year.

A buyer who pays cash and takes the house as-is can often close on a short timeline, which helps when a tax deadline is close. Bring the parcel's tax map number and your deed information when you call. If a lender holds a mortgage, tell the lender about the delinquency early, so the payoff and the mortgage satisfaction can be lined up for the same closing day.

Town collectors take current county and town tax early in the year. After that, the Fulton County Treasurer takes over whatever is still unpaid. The Treasurer's office is in the County Office Building at 223 West Main Street, Room 202, Johnstown, NY 12095, phone (518) 736-5580. Hours are Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm, and 9 am to 4 pm from July 1 through Labor Day.

The Treasurer collects delinquent school, village, town and county taxes and runs the foreclosure and auction process under the state Real Property Tax Law. It works alongside the town tax collectors. It also collects and enforces taxes on parcels in the City of Gloversville, but it does not collect City of Johnstown taxes, so a Johnstown owner pays the city.

The Real Property Tax Service Agency, at (518) 736-5507 in the same building, keeps the tax maps. Its online Beacon map shows ownership, property inventory and assessed value, refreshed nightly. It also gives the parcel's SBL (section, block, lot) number, the same number printed on tax bills and assessment rolls. Look yours up before you call anyone, because every office will ask for it.

Payment windows and where to pay

Each tax has its own window. County and town tax is due early in the year, school and village tax come in the fall, and the City of Gloversville keeps its own calendar.

Fulton County payment windows
TaxPay toWindow
County and townTown collectorJanuary 1 to March 31
Unpaid county and townCounty TreasurerReturned April 1, collections begin May 1
VillageVillage collectorJune 1 to October 31
School (town districts)School tax collectorSeptember 1 to October 31
City of GloversvilleCity, then TreasurerApril 1 to October 31, Treasurer from December 1

Village and school payments are not accepted after October 31, and unpaid town, school and village amounts are relevied on the next county bill. Current county tax cannot be paid during the first two weeks of April while the books transfer, so call the Treasurer in the last week of April for the amount due. Online payments for delinquent town tax open at the end of April. Mailed payments go to P.O. Box 128, Johnstown, NY 12095, and never as cash.

Installment plans for back taxes

Fulton County offers one, but only in May. Local Law No. 2 of 1997 lets the Treasurer sign installment agreements with owners of residential real property, and the county processes them only from May 1 through May 31. Letters go out in April to qualified owners who are behind.

  • The down payment is 25% of the eligible delinquent taxes.
  • Payments are monthly, and the term cannot exceed 24 months.
  • Eligible taxes in the most recent window were the prior year's county tax and the school and city tax from the year before that.
  • Commercial property and land are not eligible.
  • A parcel foreclosed on within the last three years, or one that defaulted on an installment agreement in the last three years, is not eligible.

Call the Treasurer to confirm whether you qualify. If you miss this May, the next chance is May 2027. Owners who are behind and thinking of selling should ask about the plan first, since a signed agreement and a written balance make it easier for a title company to close.

Foreclosure and old liens

The Treasurer's office handles the foreclosure and auction steps, so anyone with a lien that old should call (518) 736-5580 or email fctreasurer@fultoncountyny.gov before listing a house. In the latest round, owners with unpaid school, city and county taxes from several years back were given a last day to redeem, and that date came in November 2025.

The rules for redeeming are the same each round. All taxes must be paid in full in reverse chronological order by year, with guaranteed funds. Ask the Treasurer for a Parcel Status Report to learn the exact amount owed. Owners can pay at the Treasurer's office or by card online. The county also points people toward the New York State Homeowner Assistance Fund for help with delinquent taxes.

What to know about Fulton County housing

Fulton County is in the Mohawk Valley. Johnstown is the county seat and Gloversville is the largest city. Population has slipped from 55,531 in 2010 to an estimated 52,216 in 2025, across 28,418 housing units. Owners live in 71.4% of homes. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $163,100, typical monthly rent is $912, and median household income is $66,533. Only 85 building permits were recorded in 2025, so new construction is thin and resale homes carry most of the market.

With values in that range, back taxes, interest and fees can eat a large share of a seller's proceeds, which is why checking the Beacon map and the Treasurer's balance before listing pays off.

How do I clear Fulton County tax before closing a sale?

Ask the right office for the right year. During tax collection dates you contact the local tax collector. Outside those dates you contact the County Treasurer for county and town taxes, and the city or school collector for those taxes.

  1. Find the parcel's SBL number on the Beacon map or the tax bill.
  2. Call the Treasurer at (518) 736-5580 and ask for a Parcel Status Report on any delinquent year.
  3. Pay older years first, since the Treasurer requires reverse chronological order for foreclosure redemption.
  4. Ask about exemptions, STAR and veteran or senior benefits through your assessor or the county's real property office at (518) 736-5509. STAR applications go to the state directly.
  5. Give the closing attorney the written payoff amounts.

The Treasurer's office can say which taxing districts are involved when a parcel straddles city, town and school bills. Bring the SBL number, the deed or tax bill, and any installment agreement paperwork when you call or visit. On closing day, the attorney or title company should have a current figure from each office that bills the parcel: the town or county for the early-year tax, the school collector, and the village or city if one applies. A bill paid in the wrong office can be returned, so confirm who holds each year before you send money. Timing matters too. A closing in February or March usually means the town collector still holds the current bill, while a closing after May usually means the Treasurer holds anything left over. A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands can close with the payoff taken from proceeds, which skips the wait for a financed buyer's appraisal and lender review.

Frequently asked questions

When can I pay Fulton County tax to my town collector?

January 1 through March 31. After that the town collector returns unpaid bills to the County Treasurer, and the Treasurer's office begins collections on May 1.

Is there a Fulton County installment plan for back taxes?

Yes, for eligible owners of residential property, but agreements are processed only in May. The down payment is 25% of the eligible delinquent tax, the term is up to 24 months, and payments are monthly.

Does the Fulton County Treasurer collect City of Johnstown taxes?

No. The Treasurer does collect City of Gloversville parcels, but for City of Johnstown taxes you contact the city.

How do I find a Fulton County parcel's tax map number?

Use the Beacon online map from the Real Property Tax Service Agency. It shows the SBL, also called the tax map number, along with ownership and assessed value. The same number appears on tax bills and assessment rolls.

How do I apply for STAR in Fulton County?

Apply directly with New York State. Owners now register with the state, and the state number is (518) 457-2036.

Which Montgomery County office handles delinquent property tax?

The Montgomery County Treasurer handles delinquent taxes, from the County Annex Building at 20 Park Street in Fonda (mailing address PO Box 1500, Fonda, NY 12068). The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM, and the phone number is 518-853-8175.
