  • Assessment, tax roll or rate question: Real Property Tax Department.
  • Value dispute: your town or city assessor and its Board of Assessment Review.

Sort out which office owns the question before you call, because the Treasurer cannot change an assessment and the assessor cannot quote a payoff. A seller with an overdue bill usually needs both: the Treasurer for the balance, and the assessor or the rolls to see whether the value looks right before listing. Write down each answer with the date and the name of the office, and pass the written figures to the closing attorney.

Montgomery County housing at a glance

Montgomery County is a Mohawk Valley county with Fonda as its seat, along the Mohawk River and the Erie Canal corridor west of Schenectady and northwest of Albany. It covers about 403 square miles of land, and its population is estimated at 50,046 in July 2025, up 1.0% from the 2020 base.

The county has ten towns: Amsterdam, Canajoharie, Charleston, Florida, Glen, Minden, Mohawk, Palatine, Root and St. Johnsville. The City of Amsterdam sits inside it, along with villages such as Fort Plain, Fultonville, Canajoharie and Palatine Bridge.

Housing is inexpensive here. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $157,500, owners occupy 70.4% of homes, median household income is $64,943 and median gross rent is $940. There are 23,243 housing units. Only 105 building permits were issued in 2025, so there is little new construction competing with resale homes. At these prices, a few years of back tax, interest and fees can take a big bite out of what a seller nets.

When are Montgomery County grievance days?

Most Montgomery County towns hold Grievance Day on the fourth Tuesday in May, while the City of Amsterdam holds its own on the third Tuesday in January. A few towns shift by a few days.

In 2027 that puts the City of Amsterdam on January 19 and the fourth-Tuesday towns on May 25.

How the City of Amsterdam calendar differs

The City of Amsterdam assesses on a winter schedule that runs ahead of the towns by months. Its valuation date and taxable status date are both December 1, the tentative roll is filed January 1, and the final roll is filed March 1.

The city's judicial deadlines follow. A small claims assessment review application and an Article 7 certiorari filing are both due March 31, which is 30 days after the final roll is filed. A homeowner must go before the Board of Assessment Review first to use small claims. City tax bills and Greater Amsterdam School District bills go out July 1, while county tax bills go out January 1 based on the final roll.

If your home is inside the city, the appeal window opens each January, so a seller who misses it waits a year. Sellers in a town have more time, since the May Grievance Day comes later.

When the county posts rolls and rates

Assessment and tax data go up on the Real Property site in a steady yearly pattern, which tells you when a value or rate figure is likely to be online.

  • Tentative assessment rolls for the towns appear in early May.
  • Final assessment rolls follow in early July.
  • Village tax rates are posted around June, and City of Amsterdam rates in July.
  • School district tax rates appear in September.
  • Town and county tax rolls and rates, plus the city's tentative roll, appear in early January.

Use these postings to check your parcel before you list. A seller who looks up the roll in May and the rate in January can estimate the next bill with real numbers, rather than guessing from last year's.

How can I sell a Montgomery County home with property tax owed?

Call the Treasurer in Fonda and ask for a payoff figure on your parcel, then compare it with an offer. State law gives you a defined period to pay. Under RPTL 1110, a property with a delinquent lien can be redeemed by paying the lien and the charges authorized by law, and the period ends two years after the lien date unless the published notice names a later date.

A sale that pays cash and accepts the house as it stands can close faster than a retail listing, which matters when you want the balance cleared before it grows. With the median home valued near $157,500, fast action keeps fees from outrunning your equity.

If you plan to contest value before selling, homeowners in towns can prepare for May 2027 by pulling the town's tentative roll when it posts in early May, gathering recent sales of similar homes, and getting an appraisal if the figure looks far off. There is no cost to grieve and no need for a lawyer, and you can only challenge the assessment on the current tentative roll, not past years.

  2. Check your town's or the city's assessment calendar for any open appeal window.
  3. Pick a closing date with enough time for the balance to be paid from proceeds.

Have your parcel number and a recent tax bill in hand when you call. If you inherited the house or the deed is still in a relative's name, say so up front, since the Treasurer will need to know who can pay and sign.

Also ask whether any earlier years are open, not just the current one, and and ask the closing attorney to confirm the payoff in writing before the closing date is set.

Where is the Montgomery County Treasurer's office?

It is in the County Annex Building at 20 Park Street, Fonda, NY 12068 (PO Box 1500). Hours are Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM, and the phone number is 518-853-8175.

When is Grievance Day for a Montgomery County town?

In most towns it is the fourth Tuesday in May, which is May 25, 2027. Charleston, Glen, St. Johnsville and the Town of Amsterdam use dates a few days later, and the City of Amsterdam uses the third Tuesday in January.

Do I have a time limit to redeem a tax lien in Montgomery County?

Yes. RPTL 1110 sets the redemption period at two years after the lien date, unless the published notice gives a later date or a tax district has adopted a different period for certain properties.

When do Montgomery County tax bills go out?

Who bills property tax in Queens

Since 1899 Queens has been coextensive with Queens County, so the county has no separate government. The New York City Department of Finance bills property tax in Queens and values every parcel in the borough, identifying each by borough, block and lot. The Queens Business Center of the Department of Finance is at 144-06 94th Avenue, first floor, and 311 answers general questions.

The borough has an estimated 2,358,182 residents and 934,750 housing units, and only 44.9 percent of housing is owner-occupied. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $723,800, which puts a tax debt of $5,000 in perspective even though daily compounding at up to 16 percent makes a large bill grow fast.

Due dates and discounts

The city's tax year runs from July 1 to June 30. A property assessed at $250,000 or less is billed quarterly, and anything above that is billed twice a year.

Payment schedule by assessed value
Assessed valueBillingDue dates
$250,000 or lessQuarterlyJuly 1, October 1, January 1, April 1

Quarterly payers have a grace period through the 15th of the due month. With the next date being January 1, 2027, a payment postmarked by January 15 is interest-free for a quarterly property. A weekend or holiday moves a due date to the next business day.

Paying the rest of the year early earns a discount of 0.50 percent in July, 0.33 percent in October and 0.17 percent in January. If you prepaid part of the year, ask your attorney whether that payment is credited at closing.

How much does a late payment cost?

Interest on late tax compounds daily and is set each fiscal year by local law and depends on assessed value. For July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 the rates are:

  • Assessed value up to $250,000: 6 percent a year.
  • Over $250,000 up to $450,000: 9 percent.
  • Over $450,000: 16 percent.

An owner is responsible for paying on time even when no bill arrives, so confirm that Finance has your current mailing address. For tax class 2 properties with more than ten units and all class 4 properties, interest is based on the actual assessed value before phase-in. Finance also runs payment agreements and a program called PT AID, which lets eligible homeowners defer tax or pay a percentage based on income.

What is the Queens tax lien sale?

New York City sells liens on unpaid property tax to a single authorized buyer. This is not a sale of the house, but the buyer can start foreclosure within one year after the sale date if the lien is not paid or put under a payment agreement.

After a sale you owe the tax plus a 5 percent surcharge, daily compounding interest at 6, 9 or 16 percent by assessed value, and administrative costs that include an estimated $300 for notices. The city notifies owners by mail within 90 days of the sale, and the owner then deals with the new lienholder named in the letter, not with anyone who calls unprompted.

  • One-family owner-occupied homes become eligible with $5,000 or more of property tax debt that is three years overdue.
  • Two to three family homes have the same property tax test, plus a $3,000 water and sewer test at one year.
  • Residential condos and co-ops use $5,000 and three years for property tax.
  • Active duty military personnel may ask to be excluded.

Owners whose primary residence is the Queens property, who own no other New York City property, and whose combined annual income is no more than $110,750 may apply to waive the 5 percent surcharge.

How do I challenge a Queens assessment?

Finance sends a Notice of Property Value around January 15 each year. It carries the estimated market value, the tentative assessed value, the tax class and any exemptions. If the property facts are wrong, Finance corrects them. If you dispute the assessed value, tax class or an exemption, the independent Tax Commission handles that review.

You must file an Application for Correction, and the Tax Commission has to receive it by a deadline that cannot be extended: March 1 for tax class 2, 3 and 4, and March 15 for class 1. Class 1 valuation claims use Form TC108. You can file in person or by mail at One Centre Street, Room 2400 in Manhattan, or at the Queens Business Center of the Department of Finance, 144-06 94th Avenue, first floor. Filing by email is not allowed.

The 2026 tax rate for class 1 is 19.843 percent, for class 2 it is 12.439 percent, for class 3 it is 11.108 percent and for class 4 it is 10.848 percent. Exemptions such as STAR, senior citizen, military service and disability can be reviewed on separate forms with a May 31 deadline.

Selling a Queens house when tax is overdue

Ask the Department of Finance for the amount you owe and whether your parcel was included in a lien sale. Call 311 if the bill is unclear. If a lien was sold, the payoff goes to the new lienholder named in the city's letter, while current charges still go to the city.

  1. Pull a statement for the borough, block and lot and match it to your closing date.
  2. Learn whether any water or sewer debt sits on the same account.
  3. Close your STAR registration if you have one, and keep any assessment appeal papers for your attorney.
  4. Pay all debts from the sale proceeds at the closing table through your attorney.

A cash buyer will take a Queens house with arrears, repairs and tenants, and can close faster than a financed buyer who needs an appraisal. Ask for the offer in writing before you set a date.

Bring the borough, block and lot, your latest Finance bill, any lien sale letter, and your assessment appeal papers if you filed one. Finance can tell you whether the account has quarterly or semi-annual billing, which affects how much of the current period you have already paid and how your attorney splits the bill at closing. If you prepaid, ask the attorney to confirm the credit in writing so the closing statement matches the Finance record.

Who bills property tax in Queens County?

The New York City Department of Finance bills it. There is no county treasurer or town collector, because Queens has been coextensive with the county since 1899. The Queens Business Center is at 144-06 94th Avenue, first floor, and 311 handles questions.

When is the next Queens property tax payment due?

The next due date is January 1, 2027 for quarterly and semi-annual payers. Quarterly payers get a grace period through January 15. If the due date falls on a weekend or federal holiday, payment is due the next business day.

What interest rate applies to late Queens property tax?

The rate is 6 percent for assessed value up to $250,000, 9 percent from there to $450,000 and 16 percent above $450,000, from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. Interest compounds daily, so late payments cost more each day.

Can the city sell my house over unpaid tax in Queens?

The city sells the debt, not the house, in a lien sale to an authorized buyer. That lienholder can begin foreclosure within one year after the sale if the debt is unpaid and no payment agreement exists. One-family owner-occupied homes qualify for sale with $5,000 of tax debt three years overdue.

How do I appeal my Queens assessed value?

File an Application for Correction with the Tax Commission. It must be received by March 1 for tax classes 2, 3 and 4, or March 15 for class 1, and filing is in person or by mail. Use Form TC108 for a class 1 valuation claim.
